description: Friction is the force that opposes relative motion between surfaces in contact, covering its causes, types, laws, the coefficient of friction (mu = F/R), and ways to increase or reduce it in everyday and engineering applications.

options.text: A force that helps objects move faster
A force that opposes relative motion between two surfaces in contact
A force that pulls objects towards the Earth
A force that acts only on moving cars

mcq.explanation: Friction is the force that resists or opposes the relative motion (or tendency of motion) between two surfaces in contact.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a main cause of friction between two solid surfaces?

options.text: The temperature of the air only
Roughness and interlocking of tiny bumps on the surfaces
The weight of the air above the object

mcq.explanation: Even surfaces that look smooth have tiny bumps and hollows; these interlock and resist sliding, causing friction.

mcq.questionText: The friction that acts on an object that is moving (sliding) over a surface is called:
mcq.explanation: Kinetic, or sliding, friction acts between surfaces that are already moving relative to each other.

mcq.questionText: The maximum value of static friction, reached just before an object starts to move, is called:
mcq.explanation: Limiting friction is the greatest static friction that acts on a body just at the point of starting to slide.

mcq.questionText: The coefficient of friction is defined by the relationship:
mcq.explanation: The coefficient of friction mu equals the friction force F divided by the normal reaction R, so mu = F/R.

mcq.questionText: The normal reaction (R) acting on a block resting on a flat horizontal table is:

options.text: Equal and opposite to the weight of the block

mcq.explanation: On a horizontal surface the normal reaction balances the weight, so R = mg, acting perpendicular to the surface.

mcq.questionText: Which of these is an ADVANTAGE of friction?

options.text: It causes wear and tear of machine parts
It allows us to walk without slipping
It reduces the efficiency of engines

mcq.explanation: Friction between our feet and the ground gives the grip needed to walk; without it we would slip.

mcq.questionText: Which method is used to REDUCE friction in machines?

options.text: Using ball or roller bearings and lubricants

mcq.explanation: Ball/roller bearings replace sliding with rolling, and lubricants form a film that keeps surfaces apart, both reducing friction.

mcq.questionText: A block weighing 50 N rests on a horizontal floor. The friction force needed to just start it moving is 20 N. What is the coefficient of friction between the block and the floor?
mcq.explanation: On a horizontal floor R = weight = 50 N. So mu = F/R = 20/50 = 0.4.

mcq.questionText: A box rests on a table where R = 80 N and the coefficient of friction is 0.3. The friction force is:
Streamlining the shape of cars and aeroplanes is mainly done to:

options.text: Reduce friction (air resistance) as they move through air

mcq.explanation: A streamlined shape lets air flow smoothly around the body, reducing fluid friction (drag) and saving fuel.

mcq.questionText: Why are tyres and the soles of shoes made with treads (grooves)?

options.text: To reduce friction with the ground
To increase friction and improve grip
To make them look attractive only

mcq.explanation: Treads increase grip by raising friction, especially on wet or slippery ground, helping to prevent skidding.

mcq.questionText: Compared with sliding friction, rolling friction is generally:
mcq.explanation: Rolling friction is much smaller than sliding friction, which is why wheels and bearings make movement easier.

mcq.questionText: According to the laws of friction, the friction force between two surfaces depends mainly on:

options.text: The area of contact between the surfaces
The normal reaction and the nature of the surfaces

mcq.explanation: Friction is proportional to the normal reaction and depends on the nature of the surfaces, but is largely independent of the contact area.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a DISADVANTAGE of friction?

options.text: It helps a nail to stay in wood
It causes machine parts to wear out and waste energy as heat
It allows us to hold objects

mcq.explanation: Friction wears out moving parts and converts useful energy into heat, lowering the efficiency of machines.

fib.questionText: The force that opposes the relative motion between two surfaces in contact is called _____.
fib.explanation: Friction always acts to oppose motion or the tendency of motion between contacting surfaces.

fib.questionText: The force acting perpendicular to a surface and supporting an object resting on it is called the _____ reaction.
fib.explanation: The normal reaction (R) acts at right angles to the surface in contact.

fib.questionText: The coefficient of friction is calculated using the formula mu = _____ / R.
fib.explanation: The coefficient of friction equals the friction force F divided by the normal reaction R.

fib.questionText: The friction that acts on a stationary object that is not yet moving is called _____ friction.
fib.explanation: Static friction acts on a body at rest and can vary up to the limiting value.

fib.questionText: The greatest value of static friction reached just before an object begins to slide is called _____ friction.
fib.explanation: Limiting friction is the maximum static friction at the point of slipping.

fib.questionText: Applying oil or grease between moving parts to reduce friction is called _____.
fib.explanation: Lubrication forms a thin film between surfaces, keeping them apart and reducing friction and wear.

fib.questionText: The coefficient of friction mu has no _____ because it is a ratio of two forces.
fib.explanation: Since mu = F/R divides one force by another, the units cancel and mu is just a number.

fib.questionText: Replacing sliding contact with rolling contact in machines is done using ball or roller _____.
fib.explanation: Bearings use rolling balls or rollers to greatly reduce friction in rotating parts.

fib.questionText: A block of weight 60 N rests on a horizontal floor with mu = 0.5. The friction force needed to move it is _____ N.
fib.explanation: On a horizontal floor R = 60 N, so F = mu x R = 0.5 x 60 = 30 N.

fib.questionText: Friction between machine parts often produces unwanted _____, which is a waste of energy.
fib.explanation: Work done against friction is converted into heat, raising the temperature of the parts and wasting energy.

tf.questionText: Friction always acts in the same direction as the motion of an object.
tf.explanation: Friction acts opposite to the direction of motion or the tendency of motion, not the same direction.

tf.questionText: The coefficient of friction has no units.
tf.explanation: Because mu = F/R is a ratio of two forces, the units cancel, leaving a pure number.

tf.questionText: Rolling friction is usually larger than sliding friction.
tf.explanation: Rolling friction is much smaller than sliding friction, which is why wheels make moving easier.

tf.questionText: Without friction it would be impossible to walk normally on the ground.
tf.explanation: Friction between our feet and the floor provides the grip needed to walk; without it we would slip.

tf.questionText: Lubricating oil increases the friction between moving parts of a machine.
tf.explanation: Lubricants reduce friction by forming a film that keeps the surfaces apart.

tf.questionText: The friction force between two surfaces is proportional to the normal reaction.
tf.explanation: One of the laws of friction states that F is proportional to R, giving F = mu x R.

tf.questionText: Friction is always harmful and has no useful purposes.
tf.explanation: Friction is also very useful: it helps us walk, grip objects, brake vehicles and light a matchstick.

tf.questionText: On a horizontal surface, the normal reaction on a resting block equals its weight.
tf.explanation: On a level surface the normal reaction balances the weight, so R = mg.

tf.questionText: Making the treads on a tyre deeper is a way of reducing friction.
tf.explanation: Treads are designed to increase friction and grip, not reduce it.

tf.questionText: Friction is caused mainly by the interlocking of tiny rough projections on the surfaces in contact.
tf.explanation: Microscopic bumps on surfaces interlock and resist sliding, which produces friction.

summary.correctAnswer: Friction is the force that opposes the relative motion (or tendency of motion) between two surfaces in contact.
summary.explanation: This is the standard definition emphasising opposition to motion between contacting surfaces.

summary.questionText: State the main cause of friction between two solid surfaces.
summary.correctAnswer: The roughness and interlocking of tiny projections (bumps) on the surfaces in contact.
summary.explanation: Even smooth-looking surfaces have microscopic irregularities that interlock and resist sliding.

summary.questionText: List the main types of friction.
summary.correctAnswer: Static friction, limiting friction, kinetic (sliding) friction, and rolling friction.
summary.explanation: These are the common types: static and limiting for bodies at rest, kinetic for sliding, and rolling for rolling objects.

summary.questionText: Write the formula for the coefficient of friction and define each symbol.
summary.correctAnswer: mu = F / R, where mu is the coefficient of friction, F is the friction force and R is the normal reaction.
summary.explanation: This relationship links friction force to the normal reaction through the coefficient mu.

summary.correctAnswer: Friction is proportional to the normal reaction (F = mu x R), and friction is independent of the area of contact.
summary.explanation: These are two of the basic experimental laws of friction taught at O-Level.

summary.correctAnswer: It enables us to walk without slipping and allows vehicles to brake and move (grip the road).
summary.explanation: Friction provides grip for walking, gripping objects, braking and starting motion.

summary.correctAnswer: It causes wear and tear of moving parts and wastes useful energy as heat.
summary.explanation: Friction reduces efficiency by wearing parts and converting energy to heat.

summary.questionText: State three methods of reducing friction.
summary.correctAnswer: Lubrication (oil/grease), using ball or roller bearings, streamlining, and polishing surfaces.
summary.explanation: These methods either separate the surfaces, replace sliding with rolling, or smooth the surfaces.

summary.questionText: State two methods of increasing friction.
summary.correctAnswer: Making surfaces rough by adding treads/grooves, and using brake pads or non-slip materials.
summary.explanation: Increasing roughness or using high-friction materials raises the friction force where grip is needed.

summary.questionText: What is the normal reaction, and in which direction does it act?
summary.correctAnswer: The normal reaction is the supporting force from a surface acting perpendicular (at right angles) to that surface.
summary.explanation: The normal reaction R always acts perpendicular to the surface in contact and supports the object.

hoq.questionText: A wooden crate of mass 20 kg rests on a horizontal floor. A horizontal force just makes it begin to slide when it reaches 60 N. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, what is the coefficient of friction between the crate and the floor?
hoq.explanation: Weight = mg = 20 x 10 = 200 N, so on a horizontal floor R = 200 N. mu = F/R = 60/200 = 0.3.

hoq.questionText: A box of mass 15 kg rests on a horizontal table. The coefficient of friction between the box and the table is 0.4. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, what is the minimum horizontal force needed to just start the box moving?
hoq.explanation: R = mg = 15 x 10 = 150 N. Limiting friction F = mu x R = 0.4 x 150 = 60 N, so a force of 60 N is needed to start it moving.

hoq.questionText: A block of mass 5 kg is placed on a rough horizontal surface. A horizontal pull of 25 N keeps it moving at a steady (constant) speed. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, what is the coefficient of kinetic friction?
hoq.explanation: At steady speed the pull equals the kinetic friction, so F = 25 N. R = mg = 5 x 10 = 50 N. mu = F/R = 25/50 = 0.5.
